title: Bar-parity decomposition: sinh/cosh interpretation and the c_k ladder
html:
Bar-parity decomposition: sinh/cosh interpretation and the c_k ladder

This is the algebraic core of the sinh/cosh split under the bar involution \sigma: any element — in particular \log\Phi_b for the Faddeev quantum dilogarithm — decomposes into a bar-even (\cosh) and a bar-odd (\sinh) part. The Faddeev \Phi_b additionally carries the modular double symmetry \Phi_b=\Phi_{b^{-1}}; this is a distinct involution (b\mapsto b^{-1} maps q=e^{2\pi i b^2} to its S-dual \tilde q, not to q^{-1}), and it is the structure the compact q-dilogarithm lacks — not the bar parity, which the compact form also has.

Conditional on the complex-volume conjecture conj:binding-qbeta-complex-volume, the two parts are the two faces of the complex volume \mathfrak V=\mathrm{Vol}+i\,\mathrm{CS}:

  • bar-even (\cosh) =\ \mathrm{Re}\,\mathfrak V — the hyperbolic volume / mass face, evaluated on the real-q (Rogers) saddle;
  • bar-odd (\sinh) =\ \mathrm{Im}\,\mathfrak V — the Chern–Simons / decay (\mathfrak Q_\beta) face, carried on the root-of-unity (Faddeev) saddle.

The mathematical statement of prop:phi-b-bar-parity-decomposition is unconditional; only this physical identification of the two parts invokes the conjecture.

Consequence for the c_k ladder

Because the two parts live on the two archimedean saddles, a coefficient's bar-parity predicts its anchor-behaviour: bar-even coefficients are real-q and anchor-stable, bar-odd coefficients are root-of-unity and anchor-dependent. This is confirmed on both available rungs — c_2=-1 (bar-even) is Taylor-exact, c_3 (bar-odd) swings \approx 2.375\% between the proton and muon anchors — so the ladder element factors as F(q)=F_{\text{even}}(q)\cdot F_{\text{odd}}(q) with F_{\text{odd}} the modular-double (\Phi_b) factor.
